'''Kenneth D. Poss''' (born 1971 in [[Green Bay, Wisconsin]]) is an American [[biologist]] and currently director and James W. Neupert Investigator in Regenerative Biology at the [https://morgridge.org Morgridge Institute for Research] and a professor in the department of Cell and Regenerative Biology at the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]].

== Career ==
Poss received a B.A. in biology from [[Carleton College]] ([[Minnesota]]) in 1992, and a Ph.D. in biology in 1998 from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] working with [[Susumu Tonegawa]]. Poss did postdoctoral research with Mark Keating, first at [[University of Utah]] and then at [[Harvard Medical School]]. From 2003 to 2024, he led a research program at [[Duke University]] investigating zebrafish models of regeneration, where he served as James B. Duke Professor of Regenerative Biology and Head of the Duke University Regeneration Center ([[Durham, North Carolina]]).  Poss joined the [[Morgridge Institute for Research]] in the fall of 2024. He co-founded and served as the first president of the [http://isrbio.org International Society for Regenerative Biology].

=== Research ===
Poss uses [[zebrafish]] to understand how and why [[tissue regeneration]] occurs. As a postdoc, he led the first positional cloning of a gene required for regeneration of amputated fins,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Poss|first1=Kenneth D.|last2=Shen|first2=Jiaxiang|last3=Nechiporuk|first3=Alex|last4=McMahon|first4=Gerald|last5=Thisse|first5=Bernard|last6=Thisse|first6=Christine|last7=Keating|first7=Mark T.|date=June 2000|title=Roles for Fgf Signaling during Zebrafish Fin Regeneration|journal=Developmental Biology|volume=222|issue=2|pages=347–358|doi=10.1006/dbio.2000.9722|pmid=10837124|issn=0012-1606|doi-access=free}}</ref> and he established zebrafish as a model for innate heart regeneration.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Poss|first=K. D.|date=2002-12-13|title=Heart Regeneration in Zebrafish|journal=Science|volume=298|issue=5601|pages=2188–2190|doi=10.1126/science.1077857|pmid=12481136|s2cid=7878193 |issn=0036-8075}}</ref>  The latter discovery made clear that heart regeneration occurs and is efficient in some [[vertebrate]]s, and that it could be dissected using molecular genetics using zebrafish a tractable [[Model organism|model system]]. Since then, he and his postdocs, students, and staff have created many tools to interrogate tissue regeneration.

Poss reported that [[Cardiac muscle|heart muscle]] cells, not [[stem cell]]s, are activated by injury to divide and directly replace lost cardiac tissue.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kikuchi|first1=Kazu|last2=Holdway|first2=Jennifer E.|last3=Werdich|first3=Andreas A.|last4=Anderson|first4=Ryan M.|last5=Fang|first5=Yi|last6=Egnaczyk|first6=Gregory F.|last7=Evans|first7=Todd|last8=MacRae|first8=Calum A.|last9=Stainier|first9=Didier Y. === Awards ===
Poss was a [[Helen Hay Whitney Foundation]] Postdoctoral Fellow, a [[Pew Scholar]], and a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] Early Career Scientist. He received the Established Investigator and Merit Awards from the [[American Heart Association]], the Ruth and A. Morris Williams Faculty Research Prize from [[Duke University]], and the Distinguished Achievement Award from [[Carleton College]]. In 2019, Poss was named a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].
